messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated KV cache memory growth + tail latency spike in prod-us-west-2. Detector: kv-cache-guardrail (p95 RPS anomaly). Service: batch-scheduler / continuous-batching. Auto-runbooks: kv-cache-oom, pack-shed-fairness. Link: https://redwood.internal/alerts/1865054321 :rotating_light:

maria (oncall): seeing 95th token latency jump to ~2.4s and a rapid increase in total KV entries from 120M -> 320M in ~8m. Paging activity up 5x. Customers showing 5xx in front-ends. @elaine can you confirm customer impact?

elaine (cs): DataWare reporting intermittent 503s for embedding jobs started ~15:03 PDT, volume ~2% of their requests but blockers for a few pipelines. They're asking if this is on our side.

arpit (eng-runtime): I pushed a minor scheduler change 2h ago that adjusted fairness weights for short-vs-long request bins (PR #4126). It deliberately increased packing density for short requests; I'm worried it increased head-of-line on large streaming requests causing continuous-batching KV footprint to blow up. Rolling that back is possible immediately.

jonas (sre): TL;DR: mixed workload -> scheduler favored short requests -> long streams got batched into same GPU instances without releasing KV cache fast enough -> cache blowup + paging thrash -> tail latency spike. Paging metrics: read_io_wait increased, page-ins doubled, and eviction churn high.

priya (prod-eng): Can we take a quick mitigation: 1) disable continuous batching on affected model pools, 2) apply a temporary packing cap in scheduler (max batch size 64 -> 32), 3) throttle prefetch. Which is lowest-risk?

arpit (eng-runtime): Disable continuous batching per pool is lowest risk. Command to toggle: ```
# disable continuous batching for model-pool: llm-prod-usw2-1
redwoodctl pool update llm-prod-usw2-1 --continuous-batching=false
```

maria (oncall): I'll run the disable now on the busiest pools while arpit prepares the rollback PR. Executing: ```
> redwoodctl pool update llm-prod-usw2-1 --continuous-batching=false
Updating pool llm-prod-usw2-1... OK (applied to 12 nodes)
```

incident-bot: NOTE: Runbook step completed: continuous-batching disabled for llm-prod-usw2-1 by maria (oncall) at 1865054402.

jonas (sre): within 90s we should see KV growth slow. Paging IO should drop. Keep an eye on page_fault_rate and evictions/sec.

(2m later) arpit (eng-runtime): started rollback PR #4128 to restore previous fairness weights. I can hotpatch scheduler in prod if approved. Patch involves reducing short-request bias by 30%.

elaine (cs): telling DataWare this is an ongoing prod incident; mitigation in progress, they should see reduction in errors in ~5-10m.

maria (oncall): metrics: KV total entries plateauing and now trending down. p95 tokens dropped back to ~700ms. DataWare reporting fewer 503s. Good so far.

arpit (eng-runtime): preparing hotpatch: ```
# hotpatch scheduler -> adjust bin_weights
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/scheduler/hotpatch \
  -d '{"pool":"llm-prod-usw2-1","bin_weight_delta": {"short": -0.3, "long": +0.3}}' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN'
```

priya (prod-eng): hold on hotpatch until we confirm full rollback PR passes quick safety checks. If continuous-batching disable keeps stable, schedule hotpatch during a low-traffic minute.

deploy-bot: deploy started: rollback-pr-4128 -> canary on llm-prod-usw2-1 (3/12 nodes). CI: green.

jonas (sre): watch the canary for increased evictions or any regression in short-request latency. Canary window 3m.

(4m later) deploy-bot: canary passed. rolling to remaining nodes (9/12)

arpit (eng-runtime): rollback fully applied at 1865055138. Scheduler weights restored to pre-PR values.

incident-bot: ACTION: post-mitigation check start. Recommended checks: page_fault_rate, evictions/sec, p95 token latency, paging IO. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache.

maria (oncall): running post-check script: ```
redwood-metrics query --range=10m "sum:kvcache.entries{pool=llm-prod-usw2-1} by (pool)"
```
Result: plateaued and slowly decreasing. p95 tokens ~550ms now. Paging io back to baseline.

elaine (cs): DataWare: "errors almost gone, thanks. We'll keep an eye on a few long jobs." They requested timeline of root cause and ETA for permanent fix.

priya (prod-eng): root cause summary for CS: scheduler weight change increased packing of short requests onto same instances; long streaming requests retained KV caches longer causing eviction thrash and paging; continuous-batching exacerbated retention. Permanent fix: refine fairness algorithm + add packing caps + improve KV cache soft-eviction heuristics. Target: hotfix in 48h, follow-up across other pools in 1 week.

jonas (sre): creating incident page and severity note. Severity: Sev2 (partial customer impact). Adding postmortem template and assigning owners: arpit (scheduler), priya (cache heuristics), maria (monitoring/playbook updates).

maria (oncall): Handoff note for night oncall (tonight 22:00 PDT): if p95 token latency >1s or paging_io > baseline*2, escalate to oncall and paging-sre. I'll leave detailed runbook steps in the incident doc.

incident-bot: Handoff created: incident-1865054321 assigned to maria (oncall), night-handoff at 1865055805.

maria (oncall): final: mitigation successful, customer impact reduced, rollback + continuous-batching disable applied. Leaving follow-ups for tomorrow: 1) tuning fairness algorithm, 2) KV soft-eviction policy, 3) add scheduler canary to detect packing regressions. Marking thread for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
